title: Austin's Future: Budget, Bonds & Growth
summary:
*   **1954 Budget & Fiscal Concerns:** The Council extensively discussed the proposed 1954 budget, debating future growth, critical infrastructure investments (power and water systems), and the impact of delayed property revaluation on tax revenue, noting the city's urgent need for new bonds.
*   **Strategic Infrastructure Planning:** Discussions highlighted the importance of a "ten-year plan" for city development, with calls for independent engineering studies to assess future power demands and compare options for power plant expansion (hydro-electric versus steam).
*   **Revenue Bond Refunding Action:** The City Manager received authorization to contact existing bondholders to secure options for refunding or exchanging the city's current revenue bonds, aiming to restructure the city's debt.

CITY OF AUSTIN, TEXAS
Special Meeting
December 01, 1953
2:00 P.M.
Council Chamber, City Hall
The meeting was called to order with Mayor McAden presiding. Roll Call: Present:
Councilmen Long, Pearson, Thompson, White, Mayor McAden Absent:
None
Present also: W. E. Seaholm, City Manager; W. T. Williams, Jr., City Attorney; D. C.
Kinney, Superintendent of Electric Department; Albert Davis, Super- intendent of Water
Department; C. G. Levander, Director of Public Works; J. D. Huffman, Jr., Director of
Finance.
The City Manager presented to the Council a tentative draft of the proposed budget for the
period beginning January 1, 1954, and ending September 30, 1954; and proposed expenditures
for the period October 1, 1954 through December 31, 1954. (Copy on file in City Clerk's
Office under Budget, 1954) Discussion was held on the tax collections for the last three
months of the year. Councilman Long felt that the budget tied in with the ten year plan,
and was not ready to adopt a ten year plan without having a competent engineering firm to
study (1) the prospective growth and demand; (2) the availability of surplus power to be
purchased and the relative merits of the hydro-electric and steam plant; and (3) the
economical feasibility of the results of the program. The City Manager pointed out that
Burns & McDonnell, Consulting Engineers, made a study of the Power Plant and Water
Distribution System, the study to cover the next several units. The only thing not studied
by outside engineers was the electric distribution system, which the City engineers were
capable of handling.
He explained the accrued depreciation on the electric distributon and water systems due to
the fact that during the war years and even up to the present time it was not possible to
get certain materials, and there was a limited amount

of money to spend, and then there was the money that went into the general fund.
Councilman Thompson made inquiry about the revaluation of the property that was delayed
another year. The City Manager reported on the revaluation in that it was for the purpose
of equalizing values, and the Council would determine the assessed valuations. Councilman
Thompson noted there was nothing could be done about collecting additional tax revenue
next year; that the Council could adjust tax rates to increase tax revenue of the city. He
noted the small amount of surplus which would not include the committments made on water
improvement in South Austin. He noted the necessity of voting bonds to relieve the budget
of some of these expenditures, or shutting down the business. Councilman Long submitted a
list of questions regarding appropriations and unfinished projects, and stated there was
spending above appropriations set out. (List of Questions on File in City Clerk's Office
under BUDGET, 1954) The City Manager discussed. the budget in detail.
Discussion of bond needs and the appointment of a committee was held.
The City Manager suggested getting in touch with MR. WINSTON JACKSON, and get him to
contact the bondholders of the City's revenue bonds and get a commitment from them on the
City's recalling the bonds. The City Manager wanted Council action on getting these
commitments through Mr. Jackson. Councilman Thompson moved that the City Manager be
authorized to contact the bondholders of our present revenue bonds with the object of
securing options whereby these bonds can be refunded or exchanged if other revenue bonds
are authorized and issued. The motion, seconded by Councilman Pearson, carried by the
following vote: Ayes: Councilmen Pearson, Thompson, White, Mayor McAden Noes: None
Present but not voting: Councilman Long
The Mayor stated there were 30 people left off the pay increase this year and suggested a
five percent increase across-the-board raise. No action was taken at this time.
Councilman White inquired about vacant property owned by the City. Councilman Thompson
asked that a list of city-owned property be compiled and furnished the Council.
There being no further business, the Council adjourned at 6:00 P.M. ATTEST:
Ban Nolly
